entities.summary: Al-Marwani Mosque or simply Marwani Mosque is an underground vaulted prayer hall in the Al-Aqsa mosque compound in Jerusalem. It is 600 square yards in area, and is located under the southeastern corner of the compound, 12.5 m (41 ft) below the courtyard, and features twelve rows of pillars and arches. In December 1996 the Jerusalem Waqf renovated the area. The area was known to the Crusaders as Solomon's Stables, the name by which it was also officially known until 1996 and still colloquially known today, and to earlier Muslims as the Old Mosque.
